# West Coast Capital Mortgage: real estate investor loans (full text)

> Private lending for real estate investors in California, Florida and Texas. Loans close with West Coast Capital Mortgage Inc. (150 E Olive Ave, Unit 112, Burbank, CA 91502; NMLS #2817729; CA DRE Corporation License #02440065) and are funded by its private lender partner. Figures are program maximums as of November 5, 2026; not a commitment to lend.

Site summary and other sections: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/llms.txt

## Private Lending for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/investor-loans

Fix and flip, construction, bridge and rental loans in California, Florida and Texas. Your loan closes with West Coast Capital Mortgage: our term sheet, our team and our borrower portal, with our private lender behind every loan.

Questions and answers:
Q: What investor loans do you offer?
A: Fix and flip, ground-up construction, bridge, single-rental DSCR, rental portfolio and multifamily bridge loans for investors buying, building and holding property in California, Florida and Texas. The loans close in your LLC or corporation, and one deal can go from the purchase and rehab loan to a long-term rental loan with us.

Q: Are you a lender or a broker?
A: Your loan closes with West Coast Capital Mortgage. We issue your term sheet, manage the loan from application to closing and stay your contact through draws, extensions and payoff, with our private lender behind every loan. We are licensed under NMLS #2817729 and California DRE Corporation License #02440065.

Q: How much can I borrow?
A: Fix and flip loans go up to 90% of the purchase price plus 100% of the rehab budget. Ground-up construction loans go up to 75% of the land and 100% of construction, within 85% of total cost. Bridge loans go up to 70% of value, rental portfolio loans up to 80% loan-to-value, and multifamily bridge loans run from $2 million to $5 million.

Q: Will you finance my first flip?
A: Yes. With 680+ credit, a first flip can be financed at 75% up to 90% of the purchase price depending on your score, plus 100% of a light or moderate rehab budget of up to $100,000. The property should be in the area where you live and show at least a 30% projected return, in California, or in Texas outside Travis, Harris and Bexar counties. Licensed real estate agents and contractors start with experience credit.

Q: Do you need my tax returns or proof of income?
A: Not for rental loans: DSCR and portfolio loans qualify on the property’s rent, with no tax returns, W-2s or pay stubs. Fix and flip, construction and bridge loans are sized on the property, your credit, your track record and the cash you bring to closing.

Q: How much cash do I need to bring?
A: On a fix and flip, the part of the purchase price the loan does not cover (from 10%), closing costs and one month of interest reserve; the rehab is financed at 100%. On a ground-up build, at least 15% of the total project cost (10% when interest is financed). On a rental loan, a down payment from 20%, closing costs and three months of payments in reserve.

Q: How do I get the rehab or construction money?
A: The renovation or construction budget is held back at closing. As work is completed you request a draw online in the borrower portal, an inspection confirms the progress and the funds are released. On loans of $100,000 or more, interest is charged only on the money that has actually been disbursed, not on budget still in the holdback.

Q: Is there a prepayment penalty?
A: Not on fix and flip, construction or bridge loans: pay off whenever the property sells or refinances. On DSCR and portfolio rental loans you choose the structure, from five years down to none. Multifamily bridge loans carry 12 months of minimum interest.

Q: Can I keep the property as a rental when the work is done?
A: Yes. Once it is rented, refinance into a 30-year DSCR loan on its own, or into a portfolio loan with your other rentals: up to 80% of value on a rate-and-term refinance and up to 75% cash-out after 90 days of ownership. The rental loan qualifies on the rent, not on your personal income.

Q: Are these hard money loans?
A: They do the same job as hard money: short-term, asset-based, interest-only financing for investors. The difference is that our private lender works from published guidelines, with online draw requests and no prepayment penalty on fix and flip, construction and bridge loans. More on hard money loans in California.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: Will checking my terms affect my credit score?
A: No. The first conversation and the pre-screen need no credit check at all, and when credit is pulled to issue terms and assign an underwriter it is a soft pull that does not affect your score.

Q: How fast can the loan close?
A: Timing depends mostly on the appraisal and title, so we start both right after the pre-screen. What moves a closing fastest is a complete file: entity documents, purchase contract, scope of work or plans, insurance and clear title.

Q: Which states and markets do you lend in?
A: We arrange investor loans for properties in California, Florida and Texas. In Florida and Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas (the Austin, Houston and San Antonio areas), fix and flip, bridge and construction loans need at least three completed projects and a credit score of 680 or higher (700 for construction); the loan is capped at 65% of value (after-repair value on rehab and construction loans) and cost-based leverage is 5% lower, so first-time investors are not eligible there. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible. Rural properties are not eligible for bridge, construction or rental loans, and on fix and flip loans only for investors with three or more projects, at lower leverage.

Q: What do you need to look at my deal?
A: The property address, purchase price, rehab or construction budget, the after-repair or completed value, how many similar projects you have completed in the last three years, an estimated credit score, and whether a wholesaler or a related-party seller is involved.

## Fix and Flip Loans
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/fix-and-flip-loans

Up to 90% of the purchase price and 100% of the rehab budget. Short-term, interest-only money to buy and renovate 1–4 unit homes you plan to sell or rent.

Key terms:
- Purchase price financed: Up to 90%
- Rehab budget financed: 100%, released in draws
- Loan vs. after-repair value: 70% max 75% for experienced investors (700+ credit) on purchases with loans up to $750K and rehab up to $150K; no condos or rural; outside Florida and Austin, Houston and San Antonio counties
- Loan amount: $50K – $3M over $1M by pre-screen, with 3+ projects
- Term: 12 months, interest only 18–24 months for additions and ADUs
- Prepayment penalty: None
- Credit score: From 660 680 for first-time and newer investors; 660–679 needs a 3-month interest reserve
- First flip: Light or moderate rehab with 680+ credit budget up to $100K, in the area where you live; not in Florida or Austin, Houston and San Antonio counties

Questions and answers:
Q: Can I get a loan for my first flip?
A: Yes. With 680+ credit, a first flip can be financed at 75% (under 720), 80% (720–739) or up to 90% (740+, at a higher rate) of the purchase price, plus 100% of a light or moderate rehab: up to half the purchase price, with a budget of up to $100,000. The deal should show at least a 30% projected return and be in the area where you live, in California, or in Texas outside Travis, Harris and Bexar counties. Licensed real estate agents and contractors start with experience credit.

Q: How much do I need to put down?
A: Usually 10% to 25% of the purchase price, depending on your experience and credit, plus closing costs and one month of interest reserve. The rehab budget is financed at 100% and released in draws as the work is completed.

Q: What credit score do I need for a fix and flip loan?
A: 660 for investors with three or more completed projects in the last three years and 680 for first-time and newer investors. Scores from 660 to 679 need a three-month interest reserve. Experienced investors with scores from 620 to 659 may be considered case by case with a larger interest reserve and a clean credit history — no bankruptcy, foreclosure or collections.

Q: Do I pay interest on the whole loan?
A: On loans of $100,000 or more, no: interest is charged only on the money disbursed, so the rehab budget still in the holdback costs nothing until you draw it. On smaller loans interest is charged on the full amount.

Q: How do I get the rehab or construction money?
A: The renovation or construction budget is held back at closing. As work is completed you request a draw online in the borrower portal, an inspection confirms the progress and the funds are released. On loans of $100,000 or more, interest is charged only on the money that has actually been disbursed, not on budget still in the holdback.

Q: Is there a prepayment penalty?
A: No. You can pay the loan off at any time when you sell or refinance. If the project runs long, extensions of up to half the original term are available for a fee.

Q: Can I refinance a flip that is already underway?
A: Experienced investors (three or more projects, 680+ credit) can refinance a project bought within the last year that is at least 50% complete, without cash-out, with at least a 30% projected return, only light to moderate work remaining and no default interest or extension fees in the payoff. The new loan cannot be larger than the current payoff, and refinances are limited to 85% of value.

Q: Can I finance a wholesale deal?
A: Yes, when the assignment fee is no more than 20% of the underlying purchase price, the full contract chain is provided and the transaction is arm’s length. Deals between related parties go through a separate review.

Q: What properties can I flip with this loan?
A: Single-family homes, 2–4 unit properties, townhomes, PUDs and condos (outside Florida), from cosmetic updates to full gut renovations, plus additions, expansions and ADUs for experienced investors. Homes need at least 700 square feet (condos 500) and an existing roof and framing: a lot or a teardown is financed as a ground-up construction loan, and 5+ units as a multifamily bridge loan. Rural properties are financed for investors with three or more projects. Mobile homes, co-ops, condotels, mixed-use and luxury or unique homes are outside the program.

Q: Can I keep the property as a rental when the work is done?
A: Yes. Once it is rented, refinance into a 30-year DSCR loan on its own, or into a portfolio loan with your other rentals: up to 80% of value on a rate-and-term refinance and up to 75% cash-out after 90 days of ownership. The rental loan qualifies on the rent, not on your personal income.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: Which states and markets do you lend in?
A: We arrange investor loans for properties in California, Florida and Texas. In Florida and Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas (the Austin, Houston and San Antonio areas), fix and flip, bridge and construction loans need at least three completed projects and a credit score of 680 or higher (700 for construction); the loan is capped at 65% of value (after-repair value on rehab and construction loans) and cost-based leverage is 5% lower, so first-time investors are not eligible there. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible. Rural properties are not eligible for bridge, construction or rental loans, and on fix and flip loans only for investors with three or more projects, at lower leverage.

## Ground-Up Construction Loans
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/ground-up-construction-loans

Land plus 100% of the construction budget for builders putting up new 1–4 unit homes, with up to six months of interest built into the loan.

Key terms:
- Land or purchase price: Up to 75% with approved permits
- Construction budget: 100%, released in draws
- Total project cost: Up to 85% 90% with financed interest
- Loan vs. completed value: 70% max
- Loan amount: $50K – $3M over $1M by pre-screen, with 3+ projects
- Term: 12 months, interest only 18–24 months with a pricing adjustment
- Credit score: From 660 660 for builders with 5+ completed projects; 680 for newer builders
- What you can build: 1–4 units: homes, 2–4 unit buildings, small condo projects

Questions and answers:
Q: Can I get a construction loan before permits are approved?
A: Yes. Without approved permits the loan funds up to 60% of the land price at closing, and a catch-up draw brings it to 75% once permits are issued. An architect letter is required while permits are pending.

Q: How much experience do I need for a ground-up construction loan?
A: At least one completed ground-up project as a borrower, counted over the last three years. A licensed general contractor who has built ground-up as a contractor may qualify with pulled permits and entity documents that show ownership of the contracting company. Rental experience does not count. Fix and flip experience counts only case by case, when it includes large additions or expansions (two such projects count as one build).

Q: What credit score do I need?
A: 680 or higher, or from 660 for builders with five or more completed projects, using the score of the guarantor with the most experience. Building in a new market, in Florida or in Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas requires 700 or higher.

Q: How much cash do I need to build?
A: At least 15% of the total project cost (10% when up to six months of interest is financed), plus closing costs and one month of interest reserve. At closing the loan funds up to 75% of the land price, and 100% of the construction budget is released in draws.

Q: Can I include interest in the loan?
A: Yes. Up to six months of interest (up to 5% of the cost basis) can be financed into the loan, which raises the total-cost limit from 85% to 90%.

Q: How long is the term?
A: Twelve months, interest only. Terms of 18 to 24 months are available with a pricing adjustment, and extensions of up to half the original term are available for a fee, subject to approval.

Q: Do you finance lot splits and more than one home?
A: Yes. A loan can cover up to two properties, and a lot split can be financed with a separate completed value for each home. Builders with 20 or more completed projects can finance three or more homes with additional liquidity, a feasibility study and site-plan review.

Q: Can I refinance land I already own?
A: Yes, if you have owned it for three years or obtained the permits after you bought it, the loan being paid off is not a bridge or construction loan, and comparable sales support a value above your cost.

Q: How do I get the rehab or construction money?
A: The renovation or construction budget is held back at closing. As work is completed you request a draw online in the borrower portal, an inspection confirms the progress and the funds are released. On loans of $100,000 or more, interest is charged only on the money that has actually been disbursed, not on budget still in the holdback.

Q: What can I build with a ground-up loan?
A: New single-family homes, 2–4 unit buildings, townhomes and condo projects of up to four units on infill lots in cities and suburbs, including teardowns and lot splits, at mainstream price points. Large tracts, rural sites and luxury or unique homes are outside the program.

Q: Can I keep the property as a rental when the work is done?
A: Yes. Once it is rented, refinance into a 30-year DSCR loan on its own, or into a portfolio loan with your other rentals: up to 80% of value on a rate-and-term refinance and up to 75% cash-out after 90 days of ownership. The rental loan qualifies on the rent, not on your personal income.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: Which states and markets do you lend in?
A: We arrange investor loans for properties in California, Florida and Texas. In Florida and Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas (the Austin, Houston and San Antonio areas), fix and flip, bridge and construction loans need at least three completed projects and a credit score of 680 or higher (700 for construction); the loan is capped at 65% of value (after-repair value on rehab and construction loans) and cost-based leverage is 5% lower, so first-time investors are not eligible there. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible. Rural properties are not eligible for bridge, construction or rental loans, and on fix and flip loans only for investors with three or more projects, at lower leverage.

## Investor Bridge Loans
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/bridge-loans

For a finished property that’s listed for sale or leasing up. Pay off a rehab loan that’s coming due, or buy a finished home quickly.

Key terms:
- Loan vs. as-is value: Up to 70%
- Loan vs. your cost: 80%, or 90% with 3+ projects homes bought in the last 6 months; the lower of the value and cost limits applies
- Loan amount: $50K – $3M over $1M by pre-screen, with 3+ projects
- Term: 12 months, interest only extension up to 6 months for a fee
- Cash-flow test: None on renovated (C1–C2) homes 1.10 DSCR at exit in C3–C4 condition
- Prepayment penalty: None
- Credit score: From 660 680 for newer investors

Questions and answers:
Q: When does a bridge loan make sense for an investor?
A: When a renovated or newly built property is finished but not yet sold, when a rehab or construction loan is maturing, when you want to buy a finished property quickly, or when a rental is leasing up before it qualifies for a long-term DSCR loan.

Q: Can a bridge loan pay off my current hard money loan?
A: Often, if the project is complete: a bridge loan does not fund remaining work. Payoffs that include default interest, extension fees or penalties, properties with a lis pendens, projects showing a loss, credit scores under 660 and a bankruptcy or foreclosure in the last seven years may not qualify.

Q: How is the loan sized for a property that is listed for sale?
A: On the lower of the list price and the appraised value. Properties bought in the last six months are sized on your cost (purchase plus documented renovation); after six months of ownership, on the appraised value.

Q: Is a DSCR required?
A: Not for renovated homes in C1 or C2 condition, whether they will be sold or rented. Properties in C3 or C4 condition need a 1.10 debt-service coverage ratio at exit.

Q: Do I need experience?
A: Not for renovated homes in C1–C2 condition, with a credit score of 680 or higher. Properties in C3–C4 condition require at least one completed project in the last three years.

Q: What credit score do I need for a bridge loan?
A: 680 for newer investors and 660 for investors with three or more completed projects. Scores from 660 to 679 need a three-month interest reserve.

Q: What happens after the bridge loan?
A: You repay it when the property sells, or refinance into a long-term DSCR loan or rental portfolio loan once it is rented. There is no prepayment penalty.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: How fast can the loan close?
A: Timing depends mostly on the appraisal and title, so we start both right after the pre-screen. What moves a closing fastest is a complete file: entity documents, purchase contract, scope of work or plans, insurance and clear title.

Q: Which states and markets do you lend in?
A: We arrange investor loans for properties in California, Florida and Texas. In Florida and Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas (the Austin, Houston and San Antonio areas), fix and flip, bridge and construction loans need at least three completed projects and a credit score of 680 or higher (700 for construction); the loan is capped at 65% of value (after-repair value on rehab and construction loans) and cost-based leverage is 5% lower, so first-time investors are not eligible there. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible. Rural properties are not eligible for bridge, construction or rental loans, and on fix and flip loans only for investors with three or more projects, at lower leverage.

## Rental Portfolio Loans
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/rental-portfolio-loans

Two to ten rentals under one 30-year loan. One closing, one payment, qualified on the rent instead of your personal income.

Key terms:
- Properties: 2–10 in one blanket loan
- Loan amount: Up to $2M total from $50K per property; property value from $72K
- Purchase or rate-and-term: Up to 80% LTV
- Cash-out refinance: Up to 75% LTV
- DSCR minimum: 1.05 gross rent divided by the monthly payment
- Term: 30 years fixed or 5/6, 7/6 and 10/6 ARMs; interest-only options
- Income documents: None no tax returns, W-2s or pay stubs
- Credit score: From 660 700+ for 80% LTV

Questions and answers:
Q: Can I mix property types in one portfolio loan?
A: Yes. Single-family homes, 2–4 unit properties, townhomes, PUDs and warrantable condos can be combined in one loan.

Q: Can I sell one property later?
A: Yes. A property is released from the blanket loan by paying 120% of the loan amount allocated to it.

Q: Is there a prepayment penalty?
A: You choose the structure: five, four, three or one year, or no prepayment penalty.

Q: What credit score do I need?
A: 660 minimum, with 700 or higher needed for 80% loan-to-value. Leverage is based on the lowest middle score among the guarantors, and every owner with 20% or more of the entity guarantees the loan.

Q: What are the lease and occupancy rules?
A: At least 90% of the units must be leased, on 12–36 month leases to unrelated individuals; month-to-month is accepted after an initial lease term. Short-term and vacation rentals are not eligible in this program.

Q: How much cash do I need in reserve?
A: Closing costs plus three months of payments for a purchase or six months for a refinance, shown on two consecutive statements. Cash-out proceeds can cover up to half of the requirement. The first three months of principal, interest, taxes and insurance are also collected into reserves at closing.

Q: When can I do a cash-out refinance?
A: After 90 days of ownership. Between 91 and 180 days a new, higher value can be used only with documentation of the completed renovation.

Q: Can foreign nationals get a portfolio loan?
A: Yes. Foreign nationals can borrow up to 65% of value on a purchase or rate-and-term refinance and 60% on cash-out, with 12 months of payments in reserve.

Q: I only have one rental. Which loan fits?
A: A single-property DSCR loan. Portfolio loans start at two properties.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: Where is the portfolio loan available?
A: For rentals in California, Florida and Texas. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible, and rural or luxury properties are excluded.

## Multifamily Bridge Loans
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/multifamily-bridge-loans

Buy, renovate and stabilize a 5+ unit apartment building in California, then refinance into long-term agency financing.

Key terms:
- Loan amount: $2M – $5M one property per loan
- Purchase price: Up to 75%
- Renovation budget: 100%, through a holdback
- Total project cost: Up to 80% experienced sponsors, strong markets, in-place cash flow
- Term: 18–24 months, interest only plus two 6-month extensions, subject to approval
- As-stabilized value: 70% LTV max
- Once stabilized: 1.25x DSCR and a 9% debt yield
- Credit score: 725+ for every member of the entity

Questions and answers:
Q: What is the exit for a multifamily bridge loan?
A: The program is built for a refinance into long-term agency financing, such as Freddie Mac small-balance loans, once the property is stabilized at a 1.25x DSCR.

Q: How many units do I need?
A: Five or more, in a 100% residential building with an as-is value of at least $100,000 per unit.

Q: What experience do I need?
A: Experience owning and operating multifamily property in the same submarket, including renovation, with past projects taken to full or substantial stabilization. Sponsor references are checked.

Q: What are the borrower requirements?
A: A single-purpose LLC or corporation (newly formed, or an existing one that owns no other property) with no more than two members, a credit score of 725 or higher for each member, no bankruptcy or foreclosure in seven years, liquidity of 10% of the loan after closing and net worth at least equal to the loan amount. Foreign nationals are not eligible.

Q: What renovations can be financed?
A: Light to moderate value-add work up to about half of the purchase price. Structural work, additions, expansions and ground-up construction are not eligible.

Q: How does prepayment work?
A: You can pay the loan off at any time; a minimum of 12 months of interest is due at payoff. A 12-month interest and carry reserve is funded at closing.

Q: Where can I use a multifamily bridge loan?
A: For apartment buildings in primary and secondary markets in California, bought directly from the seller (no wholesale deals), one property per loan.

Q: What due diligence is required?
A: A commercial appraisal, Phase I environmental report, property condition report, renovation budget review, site visit, sponsor interview and monthly rent rolls.

## Hard Money Loans in California
URL: https://westcoastcapitalmortgage.com/hard-money-loans

Short-term private money for California real estate investors: buy, fix, build or bridge a 1–4 unit property, with the loan closed in your LLC. Also available in Florida and Texas.

Key terms:
- Programs: Fix and flip, bridge and ground-up construction plus 30-year rental refinances when you keep the property
- Purchase price financed: Up to 90% fix and flip
- Rehab or construction budget: 100%, released in draws
- Loan amount: $50K – $3M over $1M by pre-screen, with 3+ projects
- Term: 12 months, interest only no prepayment penalty
- Credit score: From 660 680 for first-time and newer investors
- Where: Statewide in California also Florida and Texas
- Borrower: LLC or corporation non-owner-occupied investment property

Questions and answers:
Q: Who offers hard money loans in Los Angeles?
A: West Coast Capital Mortgage, based in Burbank, offers hard money and private money loans across Los Angeles County and the rest of California: fix and flip, bridge and ground-up construction loans for investors who close in an LLC or corporation, plus Florida and Texas.

Q: Is private money the same as hard money?
A: In practice, yes. Both describe short-term, interest-only loans secured by investment real estate and sized mainly on the property and the deal. Ours are funded by our private lender, with published guidelines instead of one-off terms.

Q: How much can I borrow with a hard money loan?
A: Up to 90% of the purchase price plus 100% of the rehab budget on a fix and flip, within 70% of the after-repair value (75% for qualifying experienced investors). Construction loans fund up to 75% of the land and 100% of the build, and bridge loans up to 70% of value. Loans run from $50,000 to $3 million.

Q: Can I get a hard money loan for my first flip in California?
A: Yes. With 680+ credit, a first flip can be financed at 75% up to 90% of the purchase price depending on your score, plus 100% of a light or moderate rehab budget of up to $100,000, on a property in the area where you live that shows at least a 30% projected return.

Q: What credit score do I need for a hard money loan?
A: 660 for investors with three or more completed projects in the last three years and 680 for first-time and newer investors. Construction loans need 680, or 660 for builders with five or more completed projects.

Q: Do you check my income for a hard money loan?
A: No personal income verification. The loan is sized on the property, your credit, your track record and the cash you bring to closing.

Q: Are California hard money lenders licensed?
A: Companies making or arranging these loans in California are licensed by the Department of Real Estate or the Department of Financial Protection and Innovation. West Coast Capital Mortgage holds California DRE Corporation License #02440065 and NMLS #2817729, and you can check both on the DRE and NMLS Consumer Access websites.

Q: What does a hard money loan cost?
A: Pricing is set per deal: an interest rate, origination points and third-party costs such as the appraisal, title and insurance. On loans of $100,000 or more interest is charged only on disbursed funds, there is no prepayment penalty on fix and flip, construction and bridge loans, and one month of interest reserve is collected at closing. You get all of it in a written term sheet before you pay for an appraisal.

Q: How fast can the loan close?
A: Timing depends mostly on the appraisal and title, so we start both right after the pre-screen. What moves a closing fastest is a complete file: entity documents, purchase contract, scope of work or plans, insurance and clear title.

Q: How do I get the rehab or construction money?
A: The renovation or construction budget is held back at closing. As work is completed you request a draw online in the borrower portal, an inspection confirms the progress and the funds are released. On loans of $100,000 or more, interest is charged only on the money that has actually been disbursed, not on budget still in the holdback.

Q: Do I need an LLC or corporation?
A: Yes. The loan closes in your LLC or corporation, and the owners sign a personal guarantee. No entity yet? Set one up before closing. For closing we need the articles or certificate of formation, the EIN letter, the operating agreement and a recent certificate of good standing.

Q: Which states and markets do you lend in?
A: We arrange investor loans for properties in California, Florida and Texas. In Florida and Travis, Harris and Bexar counties in Texas (the Austin, Houston and San Antonio areas), fix and flip, bridge and construction loans need at least three completed projects and a credit score of 680 or higher (700 for construction); the loan is capped at 65% of value (after-repair value on rehab and construction loans) and cost-based leverage is 5% lower, so first-time investors are not eligible there. Lee, Charlotte, Sarasota and Collier counties in Florida are not eligible. Rural properties are not eligible for bridge, construction or rental loans, and on fix and flip loans only for investors with three or more projects, at lower leverage.
